extracted.intended_audience: TCNJ campus community (students, faculty, staff), campus stakeholders, and members of the public interested in Title IX regulations and compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Institutional informational/update page describing proposed and final Title IX regulations, the federal rulemaking timeline and processes (public comment, hearings, OIRA review), and how the college will implement, educate about, and solicit feedback on changes. It explains legal developments and campus-level responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Register public comment period (60 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the proposed rule is published in the Federal Register, it will be open for public comment for 60 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page repeatedly notes that publication in the Federal Register triggers a formal comment period—this is the primary opportunity for the public to submit written feedback that the agency should consider when finalizing the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA review/coordination of draft regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Dept. of Ed. sent the draft proposed amendments to the Dept.’s Title IX regulations to the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (OIRA) (which is the part of the Office of Management and Budget responsible for coordinating the review of all Executive Branch regulations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft regulations are reviewed within the Executive Branch via OIRA as part of the interagency/regulatory review process prior to publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR public hearing with oral and written submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR will be holding a public hearing to solicit feedback on the experience of students, educators, and other stakeholders with the 2020 Title IX regulations, and should be offering opportunities for participation by oral comments and written submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR will publish notice of the hearing in the Federal Register and will then be holding the hearing at least one month after that notice. The hearing will be open to the public and may be held over several days depending on the number of people who seek to testify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the comment period—to influence final rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The goal of the comment period was to provide the government with an opportunity to infuse the recommendations and make any necessary edits to the rule based upon the points raised by the general public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page cites the comment/review period as the mechanism by which public input (e.g., over 104,000 comments) is considered and may result in changes that are incorporated into the finalized regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Federal eRulemaking Portal and handling technical access issues
rubrics_metrics.description: The comment period reopened to the public for a 24-hr period for those that had technical issues accessing the Federal eRulemaking Portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may need to accommodate technical access problems to ensure equitable opportunity to comment; procedural fairness in submission logistics matters to the integrity of the notice-and-comment process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court-ordered change: statements not subject to cross-examination may be considered
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with the court’s order, the Department will immediately cease enforcement of the part of § 106.45(b)(6)(i) regarding the prohibition against statements not subject to cross-examination. In practical terms, a decision-maker at a postsecondary institution may now consider statements made by parties or witnesses that are otherwise permitted under the regulations, even if those parties or witnesses do not participate in cross-examination at the live hearing, in reaching a determination regarding responsibility in a Title IX grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a substantive change to how institutions may evaluate evidence/statements in grievance determinations; institutions must follow the current enforceable law as shaped by court orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX protections include sexual orientation and gender identity (Bostock interpretation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Biden Administration released a Notice of Interpretation into the U.S. Federal Register to clarify that Title IX Prohibits discrimination based on sex, sexual orientation, and gender identity. The notice states, 'Consistent with the Supreme Court’s ruling and analysis in Bostock, the Department interprets Title IX’s prohibition on discrimination “on the basis of sex” to encompass discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation and gender identity.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may interpret statutory protections in light of controlling judicial decisions; this interpretation affects who is covered by Title IX protections and therefore institutional obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Orders directing review/expansion of Title IX enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive Order 14021 directed the Department of Education to 'review all of its existing regulations, orders, guidance, and policies to ensure consistency with the Biden-Harris Administration’s policy that students be guaranteed education free from sexual violence' and to evaluate prior Title IX regulations for consistency with that policy. Executive Order 13988 expands prohibited forms of sex discrimination to include gender identity and sexual orientation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EOs can direct agencies to reassess and potentially change enforcement priorities and regulatory language, including accounting for intersecting forms of discrimination (race, disability, national origin) and higher victimization rates among LGBTQ+ students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between guidance (DCLs) and binding regulations; need for notice-and-comment
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR guidance documents (e.g., 'Dear Colleague' letters and Q&As) are essentially guidelines for institutions to follow, rather than a prescribed formula. However, previous guidance was sometimes treated as if mandatory without notice-and-comment, which critics argued lacked required procedural protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should be aware that guidance and regulations differ in legal force; binding obligations generally require notice-and-comment rulemaking, and agencies should not treat guidance as de facto law without proper procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Title IX Rule as federal law and institutional compliance obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Now that the regulations have been released, they are officially considered federal law. This means that TCNJ will have an obligation to comply with the letter of the law in its entirety in order to maintain compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When rules are finalized, institutions must revise policies and procedures to ensure legal compliance; colleges should coordinate campus and state partners to determine how to implement new requirements while honoring institutional values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional implementation: update policies, handbooks, and training
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Title IX & Sexual Misconduct, in collaboration with TCNJ’s Student Government, have created a comprehensive handbook to help the campus community understand the 2020 Final Rule requirements and how they impact TCNJ policies, practices, & procedures. When the proposed 2022 Title IX regulations go into effect, we will update this handbook accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should prepare and update written policies, handbooks, and supporting materials; make them available for download and reference; and revise them promptly when federal requirements change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Campus education and stakeholder engagement (transparency and feedback)
rubrics_metrics.description: TCNJ will share updates on this webpage and on social media platforms, seek feedback/suggestions/questions/concerns from the campus community via a Virtual Suggestion Box, offer to host live virtual Q&A sessions, and make Title IX staff available to answer questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactive communication, solicitation of stakeholder input, and educational outreach are expected institutional practices for explaining regulatory changes and how they affect campus processes and student safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation principle: preserve fairness, thoroughness, and student-centered philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: TCNJ states it will work to implement the new requirements 'in a way that preserves the fairness, thoroughness, and student centered philosophy that resonates with the College’s values.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When adapting to new regulatory mandates, institutions may aim to balance legal compliance with core institutional values (fairness, thoroughness, student-centeredness) in procedure design and training.
